entry.title: Asia Tech News Digest - November 28, 2026
entry.content:
# Source Title Summary Topics Link
1 CNA 'Nobody is going to help us': India's drone and robotics firms face hurdles amid growing military demand Border tensions and government support are driving India's drone and robotics manufacturers towards defence applications. But experts warn that reliance on imported components and unpredictable military orders could hinder long-term growth. Automation Read
2 TechAsia Grab taps five Indonesian startups for AI pilot projects The participating startups were Algobash, Dash, Fineksi, Grivy, and Sekilo. AI Read

Electronics Read

5 DigiTimes China's chip expansion stalls on two-year tool waits, and missing parts are to blame China's foundries keep adding capacity, but longer equipment lead times are starting to slow them down. SMIC says the global semiconductor equipment supply chain remains tight. Lead times for some tools have stretched to 16-24 months, and a few now exceed 24 months. Some equipment that was due this year has been pushed SemiconductorLogistics Read
6 DigiTimes Dutch tool maker Trymax deepens Japan push with Kanematsu PWS Dutch plasma equipment maker Trymax Semiconductor Equipment has named Kanematsu PWS its exclusive sales representative in Japan. The deal is a bet on Japanese power and automotive chipmakers at a time when their investment is weak. Semiconductor Read
7 DigiTimes Bank of Korea flags risks to memory chip boom Memory chip prices could fall well below current projections by 2028 if AI investment slows, financing conditions tighten, and Chinese manufacturers expand production, according to a Bank of Korea study released on November 26. AISemiconductor Read
8 TechAsia Your sales team saved time with AI. Now what? Gong explores how revenue AI can help sales teams focus on what matters. AI Read
9 NikkeiAsia Japan's JERA aims to build data centers for Anthropic, other AI players near power plants Japan's JERA aims to build data centers for Anthropic, other AI players near power plants AI Read

entry.title: Asia Tech News Digest - November 27, 2026
entry.content:
# Source Title Summary Topics Link
1 DigiTimes SpaceX million-satellite plan exposes hurdles to space-based data centers The US Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has approved SpaceX's plan to deploy one million space-based data center satellites, paving the way for AI infrastructure to extend beyond Earth. AI Read
2 DigiTimes DIGITIMES Insight: KV cache growth will not translate one-for-one into CXL memory demand The rapid growth of KV cache in AI inference will not translate proportionally into demand for CXL memory, because host DRAM usually takes the data moved out of HBM first, according to DIGITIMES. CXL becomes necessary only when host DRAM is constrained, the data is worth reusing, and the service depends on reloading it AI Read
3 DigiTimes Can AI resist temptation? Anthropic finds lower violation rates in new Claude models Anthropic has used simulated tests to assess whether artificial intelligence (AI) can resist temptation and follow rules. The results found that its new-generation Claude models still attempted to cross boundaries, but violations involving the use of external data fell substantially. AI Read
4 TechAsia Tencent Cloud explores AI tie-up with HK food giant Maxim’s The collaboration would cover cloud infrastructure, Weixin/WeChat Mini Programs, loyalty and marketing tools, and enterprise AI products. AI Read
5 TechAsia TCS survey finds Singapore firms struggle to scale AI About 67% respondents in Singapore said their organizations use AI internally or in interactions with partners, suppliers, or customers. AI Read
6 TechAsia India’s Ripik banks $14m to put AI on the assembly line Ripik’s AI products use visual information to monitor factory operations and identify problems as they occur. AI Read
7 EETAsia Kioxia GP2 SSD Targets 18 Million IOPS for GPU Memory Expansion The PCIe 6.0 SSD uses third-generation XL-FLASH to provide low-latency storage for AI workloads requiring expanded GPU memory. The post Kioxia GP2 SSD Targets 18 Million IOPS for GPU Memory Expansion appeared first on EE Times Asia . AI Read

entry.title: Asia Tech News Digest - November 26, 2026
entry.content:
# Source Title Summary Topics Link
1 TechAsia Apple pulls Chinese AI chatbot Talkie over child safety Talkie was listed on Google Play when scraped; that does not establish current availability. AI Read
2 CNA Nvidia halts chip shipments to Southeast Asia, FT reports Nvidia halts chip shipments to Southeast Asia, FT reports Semiconductor Read
3 DigiTimes Tata Electronics reportedly opens talks with contractors for phase 2 of Assam chip packaging plant Tata Electronics is lining up the second phase of its semiconductor assembly and test plant in Assam before the facility has been formally inaugurated, extending a project described as India's first indigenous semiconductor assembly and test facility. SemiconductorElectronics Read
4 CNA South Korea minister pushes longer R&D hours to keep pace with China “If we cannot apply an exception to the 52-hour workweek even for semiconductor R&D, what are we going to be able to do in other industries such as robotics and biotechnology?” Industry Minister Kim Jung-kwan says. SemiconductorBiotechnologyAutomation Read
5 DigiTimes Huawei offers free chip patent licenses to take on Nvidia Huawei Technologies is offering free patent licenses for its UnifiedBus chip interconnect technology and has set up dedicated semiconductor and artificial intelligence (AI) patent teams as it seeks to attract overseas hardware suppliers and build a computing ecosystem to rival Nvidia's. SemiconductorAI Read
6 DigiTimes US warns of memory glut as Samsung, SK Hynix expand The US has warned that South Korea's government-backed memory chip expansion could lead to a glut even as AI demand strains global supplies. The findings name Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, although memory chips are excluded from the proposed tariffs. ElectronicsAISemiconductor Read
7 EETAsia Renesas Expands ChipAgents AI Tools Across Global Design Teams Renesas is extending AI-assisted design and verification workflows across engineering teams in four regions, targeting RTL closure and analog design. The post Renesas Expands ChipAgents AI Tools Across Global Design Teams appeared first on EE Times Asia . AISemiconductor Read
8 EETAsia Edge AI Design Extends Beyond Compute to System Integration Deploying edge AI requires coordinated optimization of processing, sensors, memory, thermal design, security and long-term product support. The post Edge AI Design Extends Beyond Compute to System Integration appeared first on EE Times Asia . AI Read
9 TechAsia Will Asia lose prediction markets too? Asia’s banned prediction markets may go offshore like crypto did. Plus: fintech overtakes AI in SEA funding, and Jensen Huang's Nvidia mea culpa. AI Read

The companies plan to launch joint purchasing as early as spring 2027 to strengthen bargaini Semiconductor Read

6 TechAsia ByteDance opens Xiaodou AI agent to public testing in China Xiaodou can call restaurants or hotels using an AI voice and then report back to users. AI Read

entry.content:
# Source Title Summary Topics Link
1 TechAsia Singapore AI use hits 81%, but work clarity lags: report In Singapore, 12% use AI for at least half of their daily tasks. AI Read

AI Read
3 CNA TSMC unit seeks Texas property tax limit for proposed $22.6 billion chip making facility TSMC unit seeks Texas property tax limit for proposed $22.6 billion chip making facility Semiconductor Read

AISemiconductor Read
6 TechAsia Meta to pause $60b AI stock sale over shareholder lawsuit The plan would create non-voting Class C stock through a two-for-one split. AI Read
